subject: Renewal: reserved GPU top-up and ephemeral overflow options
messages:
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@atlasai.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal and capacity top-up — need options for overflow

Hi Ava,

We're kicking off our renewal conversation for Atlas AI (deal DL-2026-1147). Usage has increased ~3.4x the last six months and our ML infra team wants to lock in additional reserved GPUs for next 12 months. Two asks from infra:

- Add 40 additional reserved vGPU lanes in a second dedicated pool with a baseline throughput guarantee for peak business hours (US/EAST).
- Clarify your overflow policy during burst periods: we need to choose between a hard cap (no spill to on-demand) vs on-demand soft overflow with pre-agreed pricing/credits and preemption guarantees.

Attached is our Q4 usage snapshot for context. Can you propose contract language and 2 commercial options (one with soft ephemeral overflow, one with a hard cap)? We have a procurement window the week of Dec 6.

Thanks — happy to do a 30-min call if helpful.

Laura Kim
Head of Platform
Atlas AI
[attachment: Q4-usage-report.pdf (report, 220KB)]

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@atlasai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity top-up — need options for overflow

Hi Laura — thanks for the usage file, that helps a lot. Congrats on the growth — we can absolutely map out two clear paths for the renewal. High level:

Option 1 — Soft overflow (recommended for traffic variability):
- Add a second reserved pool: +40 vGPU lanes, baseline throughput SLA for 99th pct latency and sustained qps windows.
- Ephemeral on-demand spill: overflow routed to on-demand instances with a pre-negotiated per-hour rate and a buffer of "overflow credits" to cover sudden peaks. Preemption windows specified and a fallback model variant for degraded latency.

Option 2 — Hard cap (safety-first):
- Add +40 reserved lanes, no overflow to on-demand. Requests over reserved capacity will be throttled; we can include SLA credits for availability within reserved pool.

I'll attach a draft renewal proposal and a pricing grid for the two approaches. Ben and Jonas, can you review the SLA language and operational constraints so I can get a formal draft to Laura by EOD Friday?

Proposed next steps: 1) we share a redlineable PDF; 2) sync with procurement; 3) finalize commit and docuSign.

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T12:06:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: quick inputs needed on throughput guarantees & overflow pricing

Ben / Jonas — forwarding Laura's ask. Key decisions I need for the proposal:

1) SLA framing: can we commit to a baseline throughput (tokens/sec or qps) for the new pool during peak hours and tie credits to breaches? Recommended phrasing and credit calculus?

2) Overflow mechanics: can we offer a capped ephemeral buffer (e.g., 200 GPU-hours per month) plus pay-as-you-go beyond that at a fixed uplift vs on-demand list? What uplift % would be standard for preemption-tolerant workloads?

3) Ops lead time and provisioning window for +40 lanes — realistic ETA and staged activation plan so procurement knows dates.

I want to include both a commercial table and simple contract language. Tagging DL-2026-1147 so sales/ops alignment is tight.

— Ava

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-21T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick inputs needed on throughput guarantees & overflow pricing

Ava — quick thoughts from pricing:

1) SLA: We can define baseline throughput as a rolling 5-minute sustained qps target for the reserved pool during defined peak windows (e.g., 07:00-19:00 EST). Remedy: for breaches we offer credit = (breach minutes / total SLA minutes) * monthly reserved fee * 0.75. Keeps it measurable and contractable.

2) Ephemeral buffer model (recommended):
- Include 200 GPU-hours/month of overflow at the reserved rate (no uplift) as a goodwill buffer during ramp.
- Beyond buffer: on-demand at +20% uplift to account for dynamic provisioning and preemption risk.
- Also offer a monthly option to convert part of overflow consumption into additional reserved lanes at a pro-rated monthly rate.

3) ETA: Ops can stage +40 lanes in two waves: 20 active in T+10 business days; remaining 20 in T+30. If customer needs accelerated provisioning, we can offer expedited build at 1.25x provisioning fee.

Attaching a compact pricing-grid for insertion into the doc.

— Ben
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[attachment: pricing-grid.csv (table)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: quick inputs needed on throughput guarantees & overflow pricing

Ava / Ben — ops considerations from SRE side:

- Provisioning: we need a firm commit date for each wave so we can reserve capacity and schedule capacity tests. We'll require a pre-provisioning runbook signed off by Atlas infra (basic networking/vpc/subnet, KMS keys, and model weight sync windows).

- Preemption & fairness: ephemeral on-demand machines will be preemptible. We should guarantee eviction notifications with a 30s preemption hook where possible and provide a degraded-latency model variant that returns a lightweight result for interrupted sessions.

- Contract language suggestion: define "ephemeral buffer" as a monthly pool of GPU-hours and include an overflow throttling policy once buffer is exhausted: 1) soft-rate limiting for non-critical traffic; 2) allow urgent requests via a billed priority queue (higher uplift).

I'll draft a short amendment for the SLA and overlapped provisioning timelines.

— Jonas
Head of Capacity Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Renewal and capacity top-up — need options for overflow

Hi Laura — thanks for the patience. Based on usage and internal alignment, attached is a concise two-option summary and the proposed SLA/addendum language. Short summary here: 

Option A (Soft overflow — recommended):
- +40 reserved vGPU lanes (second dedicated pool).
- Baseline throughput SLA during peak window with credit calculus (rolling 5-min windows).
- Ephemeral buffer: 200 GPU-hours/month included; beyond that on-demand at +20% uplift. Preemption notifications and degraded model variant guaranteed.
- Staged provisioning: 20 lanes active T+10 business days, remaining 20 T+30. Expedited path available.

Option B (Hard cap):
- +40 reserved lanes, no overflow allowed. Requests above reserved capacity will be throttled. SLA credits apply for availability inside reserved pool.

Next steps: 1) pick preferred option and confirm staging preference; 2) procurement reviews attached redlineable PDF; 3) we push to DocuSign with target signature by Dec 10 to meet your window.

If you'd like, Ben and Jonas can join a 30-min call this Friday to walk the legal and ops bits.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this up.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Dedicated Capacity
Redwood Inference
